title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024
sponsor_context: Sponsor of H.R. 2670, the bill that became the FY2024 NDAA.
last_action: Enacted as the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024.
summary: The FY2024 NDAA created or expanded military and intelligence-community safeguards for AI acquisition, vulnerability testing, generative-AI detection, responsible use, and oversight of AI-assisted intelligence analysis.

substance_sections.title: CDAO acquisition authority
substance_sections.summary: Extends the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer's special acquisition authority through fiscal year 2029 and requires plans and demonstrations showing how it will deliver operational AI capabilities.

substance_sections.title: AI bug-bounty programs
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Defense Department to develop a bug-bounty program for foundation models being integrated into military missions and operations.

substance_sections.title: Generative-AI detection and watermarking competition
substance_sections.summary: Creates a prize competition to evaluate and transition tools that detect generative-AI content and apply or identify watermarks.

substance_sections.title: Responsible-AI plans and security strategy
substance_sections.summary: Requires responsible-AI guidance and accountability metrics, a strategy addressing generative-AI cybersecurity and adversarial uses, and plans to secure Defense Department models, data, and algorithms.

substance_sections.title: Study of vulnerabilities in military AI
substance_sections.summary: Requires a study of military-AI privacy, security, accuracy, explainability, testing, auditing, traceability, emergent behavior, and supporting test infrastructure.

substance_sections.title: Rules for AI-assisted intelligence products
substance_sections.summary: Requires the Director of National Intelligence to assess and update analytic and sourcing rules so intelligence products appropriately disclose and support the use of AI and machine-learning tools.

substance_sections.title: Intelligence-community AI policies
substance_sections.summary: Requires common policies for acquiring, using, testing, documenting, monitoring, and securing intelligence-community AI capabilities, including third-party models and data.

committee_dynamics: These provisions became law through the annual defense-authorization vehicle rather than as standalone AI statutes. H.R. 2670 was introduced as the FY2024 NDAA by House Armed Services Committee Chair Mike Rogers.
advance_rationale: Enacted law; implementation replaces advancement forecasting.

responsible_agencies: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

deadlines.requirement: Complete the responsible-AI strategy and process requirements due 120 days after enactment.
Develop the foundation-model bug bounty program, subject to appropriations, under § 1542.
Establish the generative AI detection and watermarking competition under § 1543.
Complete the military AI functionality, research-needs, privacy, security, and accuracy study due one year after enactment.

agency_status.detail: The statutory requirements are captured; a comprehensive official implementation assessment has not yet been completed for this grouped record.

GAO found that at least four Defense components used the CDAO Responsible AI Toolkit and others were piloting it. GAO identified gaps in governance and collaboration. The audit does not establish completion of the statutory § 1544 or § 1545 duties.

verification_level: Official Congress.gov record and public-law text verified; implementation status requires a dedicated agency review.
